rv.q: 'Paranormal Activity' knows what it wants to pull off and the execution is first-rate.
Barrett and Holloway come the closest I've ever seen — outside of a haunted house anyway — to achieving that same always-on-edge sensation onstage.

Wisely, for the thrilling 'Paranormal Activity' experience now on Broadway, the playwright Levi Holloway and the director Felix Barrett have jettisoned almost every characteristic of the movie franchise.

Horror plays are hard to pull off on Broadway, as Holloway's own somewhat creaky Grey House demonstrated in 2023. Activity is a much more successful fright night. Barrett, who codirected Sleep No More, leans into voyeurism and elicits excellent performances from Álvarez and Knight....

The stage version of 'Paranormal Activity' performs on an intimate and domestic scale yet delivers more thrills, chills and screams than Broadway has seen in years, and giving the franchise a legit afterlife.
That doesn't make the play a bad hang (I've had the time of my life on Star Tours), though its attempts to make itself more than just a vehicle for oohs and aahs grow tedious quickly.
Paranormal Activity shines as solid drama about a haunted past fueling marital discord that happens to have exceptional special effects.
What happens next can only be described as two hours and 20 minutes of hair-raising, heart-pounding, and bloodcurdling horror mixed with a dash of unexpected heart and humor.
Paranormal Activity is by far the best entry for horror theatre we have seen on Broadway, perhaps ever?
Holloway pretty much hits a grand slam for fright fans.

Theatergoers hoping for a sophisticated ghost story like The Weir or The Woman in Black will probably find the evening hopelessly lowbrow. But if you’re simply looking for a scary good time and can endure the frequently deafening sound level, Paranormal Activity is the show for you.
Fisher cooks up some chilling images that are wildly inventive and believable, even sitting very close to the stage.
Though playwright Levi Holloway's script falls far short of its aspirations of psychological complexity, it's as terrifying a play as has haunted Broadway in a long while.

Spare a thought for the 32BJ cleaners (now under a new contract) who must nightly contend with spilled popcorn and tiny puddles of urine left by horrified spectators unprepared for the jumps and bumps in director Felix Barrett’s marvelously sneaky production.
Ticket buyers who enjoy sensational doings such as roller coasters and horror flicks will want to check out this new attraction inspired by the Paranormal Activity film series.
But admiring how a trick was pulled off is not the same as being absorbed by the play around it.

Paranormal Activity is genuinely scary without resorting to the graphic violence of recent horror plays like Stranger Things: The First Shadow.

What Holloway has done with Paranormal Activity isn't boring, but it doesn't make for solid drama. The characters are slight, their dialogue is weak, and it doesn't amount to much more than a 30-minute Twilight Zone episode stretched to a two-hour running time.

cn.t: Critics find "Paranormal Activity" delivers effective scares and technical thrills on Broadway, though the script lacks psychological depth. The immersive horror spectacle earns screams and applause despite a thin story.

vs.sum: The August Wilson Theatre offers good sightlines from most seats, although the rake isn't steep, which can cause issues if seated behind taller patrons. The theater has average comfort with decent legroom but tight seats. Its Italian-inspired design and cozy feel enhance the ambiance, making it a pleasant venue overall. Facilities are adequate, with standard amenities and helpful staff.

acc.note: Stair lift to orchestra; elevator between orchestra and mezzanine. Infrared headsets available.
